purpose: Teach: あいかわらず/おまかせ/さがし/わかれ/しるし/さながら/すごし/段々

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはあいかわらずお仕事熱心だったぞ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was younger, he was always as devoted to his work as ever.
lines.style: Soft, reflective tone. Eyes distant, holding onto a memory. Voice warm but faintly melancholic. Unhurried pace, as if turning something over in his mind. Slight pause before speaking, gathering the thought.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お料理はおまかせでも美味しくお作りになったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your father was such a wonderful cook, even when we left everything to him, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle, affirmative opening. Warm nostalgia threaded through. Soft lilt at the end—checking in with him, inviting agreement. Unhurried, as if savoring the memory. Voice carries the comfort of long knowing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが古い手紙をさがしてらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was younger, he spent so much time looking through those old letters.
lines.style: Quieter now, reflective. Slower pace—the sadness beneath the surface. Voice carries the weight of what those letters might have meant. Gentle delivery, but with the gravity of an old sorrow remembered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご友人とおわかれの時、寂しがられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and when your friend left us, he felt that loss so deeply, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Understanding, softer than before. The 'dear' lands with genuine compassion—she sees what he's circling toward. Slow, steady delivery. Voice holds space for the grief without dramatizing it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが家紋をしるしとして大事にされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was younger, he treasured the family crest like it was his most prized possession.
lines.style: Quiet respect in the voice. Slow, deliberate pace—honoring the weight of tradition and continuity. Slight emphasis on what he valued. Nostalgic but grounded, as if the object itself holds his voice steady.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭の桜は、さながら絵画でしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and the cherry blossoms in the garden were like a painting come to life, weren't they, dear?
lines.style: Wistful agreement, but warm. Voice paints the image as she speaks it. Tender lilt on 'dear'—she's meeting him in the memory, gently. Slower pace, savoring each detail. Slight trailing softness at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと穏やかにすごしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was younger, those quiet times we spent together were so peaceful.
lines.style: Lowest energy of all his lines. Voice barely above a murmur. Long, warm breath. Pause before 'peaceful'—he's not just recounting, he's cherishing. Ends softly, as if the memory is dissolving into silence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭のお花が段々増えていったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and the garden kept growing more beautiful, year after year, didn't it, dear?
lines.style: Her most tender close. Voice almost a whisper—not sad, but deeply present. 'Dear' is a benediction. Slow, lingering pace. The 'didn't it' is not a question but a soft affirmation of all they've shared. Trails off into the warmth between them.
